definitions.standard: Anything that has mass and occupies space.
definitions.simple: Matter is anything you can touch, feel, or weigh. It is what everything in the universe is made of, like water, air, and rocks.
definitions.scientific: Matter is any substance that has mass and takes up space by having volume. It is composed of atoms and subatomic particles.

linguistics.origin: From Latin 'materia', meaning 'substance from which something is made'.

advanced_data.history: Ancient Indian philosophers classified matter into Pancha Tatva (Air, Earth, Fire, Sky, Water).

common_misconceptions: Light and heat are forms of matter. (They are not, they are forms of energy).
Air is not matter because it's invisible.
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student to close their eyes and wave their hand. The resistance they feel is air, proving it takes up space and is matter.
